candidate_identity.display_label: RULES: lemma eligibility reasoning and section-aware reinforcement learning

candidate_source_claim.worker_summary: Lemma applicability/precondition checking and conclusion utility should be separate stages; prefer exact/mechanical applicability evidence when available and evaluate utility only after applicability.
candidate_source_claim.scope_note: The worker already limits the paper to lemma judging rather than end-to-end Lean library admission.

primary_publication.title: Reliable Use of Lemmas via Eligibility Reasoning and Section-Aware Reinforcement Learning
primary_publication.published_claim_scope: Two-section learned lemma judging with precondition and conclusion-utility checks, plus section-aware GRPO masking; evaluated on held-out in-domain splits, a DeepTheorem-derived applicability-breaking perturbation suite, and several end-to-end math benchmarks.

observed: The ACL paper publishes exact prompts, batch size 128, rollout count 8, response lengths, training source counts, evaluation temperature 0.7, SC@7, and evaluation-set counts.
The paper states the training framework is based on verl and evaluation on vLLM.
The AMD GenAI publication page links the paper, while its public Code page does not list RULES as an open-source artifact at audit time.
Targeted public GitHub repository searches for the paper title / lemma eligibility section-aware RL returned no matching repository.
missing_for_exact_replay: No source-matched RULES training/evaluation repository located.
No released RULES model checkpoints located.
No exact processed training split / 744 accepted perturbation examples / 839 evaluation perturbation examples located as immutable artifacts.
No exact o3/GPT-OSS perturbation generation and validation outputs located.
No training seed, model-serving revision, optimizer schedule, checkpoint-selection trace, or raw per-example SC@7 predictions located in the paper.
No run-to-run variance or confidence intervals are reported for the headline tables.

independent_reproduction.search_scope: Fresh web and GitHub searches for the exact title, arXiv identifier, RULES lemma-judging code, and author/AMD public code listings.
independent_reproduction.note: No protocol-matched third-party rerun or failure report was located in this audit. Absence in this search is not evidence that none exists.

checks.name: max perturbation gain
checks.result: DeepMath DT: RULES 47.0 - vanilla 24.0 = +23.0 points, matching the paper's stated maximum-scale robustness gain.

checks.name: Qwen ablation delta
checks.result: Qwen2.5 DT: RULES 87.8 - two-section-onetime 73.1 = +14.7 points, matching the paper's stated ablation delta.

checks.name: CounterMATH error asymmetry
checks.result: 52 over-rejections / 9 under-rejections = 5.777..., matching the paper's 5.8x statement.

checks.name: simple unweighted E2E mean versus GRPO
checks.result: Across the six Table-1 E2E columns, per-model RULES-minus-GRPO means are DeepMath -2.35, OLMO2 -0.15, Qwen2.5 +0.17, Llama-3.1 -0.52 points. Across all 24 E2E cells, the simple unweighted mean is RULES 39.0833 versus GRPO 39.7958, delta -0.7125.

scope_corrections.assessment: The paper appropriately calls E2E transfer mixed in the analysis, but any stronger reading of 'average performance broadly better or on par' is not supported by a simple unweighted average of Table 1: RULES is slightly lower overall and lower for three of four per-model E2E means. The robust claim is perturbation-gating improvement, not broad E2E gain.

The 14.7-point comparison to two-section-onetime changes the temporal/output structure, and the GRPO baseline changes both output schema and objective. The released table does not provide a clean same-prompt/same-data ablation that removes only section-aware token masking while holding the sequential two-section protocol fixed. Therefore 'section-aware masking itself is indispensable' is stronger than the directly isolated evidence; the package of staged protocol + fine-grained alignment is better supported.

RULES uses learned precondition judgments from language-model outputs. The worker's recommendation to prefer kernel/mechanical applicability in a formal proof environment is an O-independent design adaptation, not something directly tested by RULES. Treat that adaptation as untested rather than as a reproduced paper result.

Training robustness depends materially on generated/filtered perturbations. The paper reports 84.8% model-consensus retention and small human spot checks, but without the exact accepted/rejected perturbation corpus and generation outputs a third party cannot replay the data construction or quantify selection sensitivity.

defensible_conclusion: RULES provides meaningful primary-study evidence that explicitly separating lemma precondition checking from conclusion utility, together with staged/fine-grained RL training and curated applicability-breaking negatives, improves robustness on a learned lemma-judging perturbation test. The current public artifact surface is insufficient for exact model/data replay, no matched independent rerun was located, broad E2E improvement is not supported by a simple Table-1 average, and the causal contribution of section-aware masking alone is not cleanly isolated from the staged output protocol. The worker's stronger formal-system design rule—mechanical applicability first, learned utility second—remains a reasonable adaptation but is not a reproduced RULES result.
reopen_conditions: Official RULES code or model checkpoints are released.
Exact processed train/eval perturbation corpora and generation/validation traces are released.
A protocol-matched independent rerun or failure report appears.
A same-data/same-sequential-prompt ablation isolates section-aware masking from output-structure changes.
A formal proof-assistant experiment compares learned applicability versus kernel/mechanical applicability under matched utility routing.
